result.report:
The supplied argument establishes the stated graph-cylinder theorem, with real affine coefficients, real local cycle weights, and finite rational spatial domains. This is a partial result; the arbitrary balanced-space classification remains open. No external mathematical theorem is indispensable: the relevant supporting arguments are supplied and can be reconstructed directly.

The elementary dependencies check out. The cone-section argument supplies finite generators; homogenization supplies point-plus-ray representations; elimination preserves rational variable coefficients despite real constants. The rational Jensen completion, touching-support argument, normal-cone characterization, and finite-minimum supergradient formulas have the hypotheses needed in their subsequent applications.

The graph reduction retains the actual geometry. A strictly positive kernel vector and (1) force the entire direction kernel to be one-dimensional. Consequently bivalent directions are opposite with equal weights, and branching stars have no opposite pair. Convex cells therefore project into straight chains that cannot traverse branching vertices. The scalar lemma follows from rational Jensen inequalities, endpoint secants, and the balanced small-distance vertex PCC. These establish endpoint continuity, finite outgoing derivatives, and their weighted inequality. Conversely, grouping the displacements of an arbitrary actual PCC produces a nonnegative relation proportional to the actual weights. This proves the converse for remote endpoints and real centres, without PC locality.

The partial-infimum propagation is valid for raw competitors. Rational slice supports give a covector whose infimum is finite at the selected rational graph point. Rational edge combinations and positive vertex combinations propagate finiteness throughout its component, including cycles and ends. A violating vertical recession ray would then contradict the obstacle upper bound. No continuity of a raw competitor is assumed.

The finite partial-infimum construction also checks out. Reference positivity makes the common spatial cells pointed. On each bounded strip or oriented end strip, a zero-graph recession vector can use only zero-graph generating rays. Thus (8) is the common finite domain for the obstacle and reference. Its interior contains zero, and the fixed-fibre linear growth bound proves compactness. Fibre minima occur at vertices; between projected spatial vertices those vertices run along rational spatial one-faces. This yields (9), with a fixed finite candidate set and rational dual gradients. The endpoint continuity proof correctly allows extra endpoint fibre types. Equation (10) retains the entire tail constraint, rather than replacing it with a finite truncation.

The global incidence argument is sound. The partial infimum of γ−C supplies a feasible witness: endpoint chords stay below the concave interval obstacle, and the prescribed tail lines stay below the full tail obstacle. Both replacements increase outgoing derivatives. Componentwise maxima preserve feasibility, and the compact-box maximization gives a genuinely greatest assignment. Every bounded edge of every cycle remains in this system. Elimination proves (12), including boundary continuity on D; simultaneous constant lowering justifies the asserted unbounded-below coordinate sections.

Equation (13) identifies the actual raw envelope globally. Each member of the supremum satisfies every actual cylinder PCC and lies below the obstacle. Touching supports of rational slices bound every raw competitor at rational carrier points. Shrinking rational simplices then extend this bound to every real centre. Applying it to γ−C gives the exact two-sided growth bounds, making Q itself an admissible global competitor and proving (14). This does not depend on local raising, a tree lift, or a cycle-unwinding argument.

The rational-domain step is essential and valid. Finite real-affine maxima alone would be insufficient. Here the active supergradient polytopes and outward normal cones have rational generators. The separation argument proves the constrained optimality condition (15), including boundary cases. Equations (16) and (17) then give rational point-and-ray descriptions of the full maximization regions. Their intersections are equality faces, and their node fibres agree across incident strips. Their vertices occur only over graph nodes; taking faces introduces no graph-interior vertices. Hence the resulting finite rational complex covers all possible recursive atoms.

The intersection-theory proofs retain the saturated lattice indices. In the two-dimensional quotient calculation, s/χ represents the primitive normal class modulo the ray; χ is not discarded. Substitution of the balancing equations cancels the vector sum of the first-divisor coefficients, and (6) is symmetric. Together with the refinement argument and ordinary-open locality of (5), this establishes the real recursive cycle in every dimension and on every lower face. Direct-product expansion gives the stated 2^d d!c normalization.

The PAPC verification tests every nonnegative real local balanced cycle in every positive dimension. Its incident balancing cone has rational generators. For each rational generator, the shifted inward vectors give rational endpoints of an actual PCC inside the ordinary open, and Jensen yields precisely (5). Linearity extends the inequality to all real incident weights. Thus every recursive divisor is nonnegative. The sequence P+1/j belongs to the stated real PAPC growth class, decreases uniformly, and has identical recursive measures, establishing the claimed regularization and operator domain.

Both vanishing lemmas are valid under their stated antecedents, and those antecedents are established wherever applied. In quotient vanishing, induction excludes the next divisor over each relative interior of a quotient face because the preceding cycle is supported where the function agrees with an ambient affine function. This controls all lower faces, not only maximal-face interiors. For lineality vanishing, a rational common fan retaining nonzero lineality has no zero-dimensional faces; refinement invariance transfers the zero coefficient to the original fan.

The contact proof exhausts the atoms. At a noncontact node-fibre vertex, C_x is a compact polyhedron with rational affine-hull direction, and the finite active-plane argument proves the exact germ (21). If dim C_x<m, its annihilator provides the required nonzero rational lineality. If dim C_x=m, (22) establishes coercivity and forces every interior dual point to have a strict scalar cap gap. Greatest-assignment maximality consequently forces L_v=0; continuity extends this equality throughout C_x. Strictly positive weights and concavity force every incident slope function to be affine there. Their rational gradients and the unique actual star relation produce A and the rational map B. The residual germ therefore factors through a complete rational normal fan in dimension m<d. Quotient vanishing eliminates the complete recursive coefficient. The isolated-tail-node case is correctly excluded by the same cap-raising argument. This covers junctions, inserted bivalent nodes, tail bases, and all exposed-face dimensions.

The triangle and the nonseparable example check directly. The actual bounded lengths are primitive lengths one, the leaves are primitive, and each star contains a determinant-one pair. The fibre candidates give the displayed caps. The coordinate upper bounds and nonnegative Laplacian slacks establish (27) for the complete cyclic system. Its node supergradients give exactly fourteen possible coefficients. Reconstructing the local recursion yields 2/5 and 58/25 at A, 6/25 at each of B and C over z=0, and zero at the other ten coefficients. The positive atoms total 16/5 and all are contact points. Neither program execution nor mass agreement is used as proof evidence.

I opened the [March 10 BMPS v1 PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1) and checked the reproduced PCC, PA, local-cycle, growth, regularization, envelope, and recursive-measure conventions, as well as the comparison proof of Proposition 6.13. Its literal coefficient restrictions are not transferred to the declared real extension. The cited automatic-continuity, locality, equivalence, and operator-extension theorems are not needed for this proof.

If a polyhedral graph presentation permits a full affine-line edge without vertices, make a preliminary rational bivalent subdivision before using oriented end strips. This is covered by the supplied subdivision argument and changes neither the carrier nor its weights, lattices, or PCC tests. No substantial mathematical repair is required.
